title: Efficient Weight Mapping and Resource Scheduling on Crossbar-based Multi-core CIM Systems
problem: Multi-core crossbar-based CIM systems (eFlash-based SoCs) must optimize for both latency and resource utilization. Key compiler challenges include high parallel processing overhead, suboptimal resource utilization, and inefficient crossbar array assignment for CNNs, resulting in poor latency and low array utilization.
motivation: Emerging multi-core CIM architectures require domain-specific compilers to translate CNN workloads efficiently; naive mapping leaves significant performance on the table.
method: Proposes resource scheduling strategy based on stream data processing to reduce intra-core and inter-core communication latency. Develops weight mapping strategy to maximize crossbar array utilization for CNN deployment. Applies stream-based processing to schedule data flows and reduce handoffs between cores.
key_novelty: Stream-based resource scheduling combined with weight mapping strategy for crossbar utilization maximization in multi-core CIM systems.
contributions: Stream-based resource scheduling to reduce intra/inter-core communication latency
Weight mapping strategy for CNN crossbar deployment
94.7% crossbar array usage rate on eFlash-based CIM SoC
limitations: Evaluation limited to CNNs on eFlash-based SoC; generalization to other workloads (RNNs, transformers); scalability to larger core counts; power/thermal analysis not discussed.
primary_theme: stream-based scheduling and weight mapping for multi-core CIM CNN acceleration
